label: NEJM: explanation or interpretation?
attribution: Barack H. Obama, NEJM, 2017; supplied PDF p. 2
title: Repealing the ACA without a Replacement — The Risks to American Health Care
coder_b_rationale: Synthesizes the claimed stakes of repeal without an alternative.
proposal: Prefer interpret for the disputed job: this paragraph summarizes stakes developed in the preceding reasoning. It names consequences without developing their mechanism. Assert remains compatible. This is a proposed reading, not an exhaustive reference label set.

label: HBR: orientation or instruction?
attribution: Peter F. Drucker, Managing Oneself, 1999; supplied 2005 reprint, PDF p. 6
title: Managing Oneself
coder_b_rationale: Introduces values as the next self-management question, distinguishes it from ethics, and asks the reader to examine their values.
coder_b_uncertainty: instruct: asking the question is actionable, but the test is not yet explained
proposal: Orientation and a directed self-question can coexist. Clarify whether reflective prompts count as instructions; a bare question heading and an actual request to examine oneself need contrasting examples. The distinction from ethics is limited clarification, not a complete definition of values.

label: Review: examples, definition and scope
attribution: Cathal Doyle, Laura Lennox and Derek Bell, BMJ Open, 2013; Results paragraph
title: A systematic review of evidence on the links between patient experience and clinical safety and effectiveness
coder_a_rationale: Categorizes association outcomes and limited coverage.
coder_b_rationale: Describes the table and outcome categories using concrete examples.
coder_b_uncertainty: Examples enumerate category contents; illustration is borderline.
proposal: Proposed reading: report plus qualify plus illustrate. The denominator condition limits the table claim; the listed instances illustrate category contents without establishing complete category boundaries. Different clauses perform different jobs.

label: HBR: history offered as support
attribution: Peter F. Drucker, Managing Oneself, 1999; supplied 2005 reprint, PDF p. 4
title: Managing Oneself
coder_b_rationale: Recounts the method's historical adoption and advances a causal account of institutional success, supplying a historical reason for its importance.
coder_b_uncertainty: support: the historical causal claim is asserted rather than independently established in this excerpt
proposal: Reporting content, narrative organization, a causal explanation and intended support for the preceding feedback-analysis recommendation can coexist. Mark the claim being supported, then assess the truth and adequacy of the historical reasoning separately. Neither coding set establishes historical validity.
